title: Column stock: simulate copies the whole cut history on each call, so a program cut one move at a time is quadratic

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_sim::cut::simulate` (the column engine behind `Stock::simulate`) copies the stock's whole cut history at the start of each call:

```rust
let mut history = dex.history.as_deref().cloned();
```

The history holds every cut so far. It grows with each call. A caller that cuts a program in small steps (one move for each call) thus copies a longer history at each step. The total time is quadratic in the number of moves.

Expected: the time of a program cut one move for each call is near the time of the same program cut in one call.

### Evidence

We run `camcraft-sim` from a fork as the stock engine of a batch verifier. The verifier reads the stock before each cutting move, thus it cuts one move for each call.

- A 3-axis job on a 2541 x 2100 column stock, 137,940 moves: one call takes 2 s. One move for each call ran for more than 1800 s, and we stopped it.
- With the history grown in place (below), one move for each call takes 6 s. The removed volume is the same to the bit as the one-call cut.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a column stock: `Stock::block(Backend::Column, 0.0, 0.0, 20.0, 20.0, 10.0, 0.1)`.
2. Make 4000 short feed moves across the block.
3. Cut them in one `simulate` call. Then cut them on a second, new block with one `simulate` call for each move.
4. Compare the times. The second cut is much slower, and the gap grows with the number of moves.

### Proposed fix

Take the history out of the stock, grow it in place with `Arc::make_mut` (this copies it only when another stock shares it), and put it back. On a refusal, truncate the cuts to their old count and put the history back, so the stock stays as it was (`add_ops` only appends cuts). We have this change and a pinning test on our fork. We will open a PR from a branch `issue/3819-history-in-place` if you accept the claim.

Not in scope: `carried::clip_columns_under` uses the same copy, but it runs one time for each setup, not for each move.

### Version and OS

v0.26.0 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `P3` (slow with a workaround: cut in one call), `effort:high` (stock simulation is under the safety floor).

Done means: a pinning test in `camcraft-sim` cuts 4000 moves one call at a time on a column stock. Each column top is the same to the bit as the one-call cut, and the time stays inside a linear budget.
